speaker: Doctor
text: I have received your report of increasing pain and swelling in your left knee over the past two months. That memory suggesting a urinary tract infection is unrelated to your leg symptoms, so I will focus on your knee instead. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me if you have noticed any redness, warmth, or a decrease in the range of motion in your knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like an inflammatory process; given the severity and duration, have you noticed any fever, chills, or a rash elsewhere on your body? I also need to know if you have a history of gout or recent trauma to this knee. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, and CRP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: Within normal limits; Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate: Slightly elevated; C-Reactive_Protein: Within normal limits

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show a slightly elevated ESR, which points to an inflammatory cause, though your blood count is normal and CRP is within limits. Have you noticed any joint pain in other areas, such as your fingers, toes, or back? REQUEST TEST: Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP, and HLA-B27.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Rheumatoid_Factor: Negative; Anti-CCP: Negative; HLA-B27: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The autoimmune markers for rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis are all negative. Given your age, the chronicity of the swelling, and the severe night pain, do you have any history of psoriasis, eye inflammation, or skin lesions like dactylitis? REQUEST TEST: Uric Acid level, HLA-B27 repeat if clinically indicated, and consider a Joint_Aspiration for cell count and crystal analysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The aspirate and uric acid results are still pending, so I will not rush to a final conclusion yet. Have you noticed any psoriasis skin patches, nail changes, or a history of uveitis/eye inflammation? REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_Joint_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Undifferentiated Spondyloarthropathy (likely Psoriatic Arthritis or Reactive Arthritis). The negative inflammatory markers (RF, Anti-CCP, HLA-B27) and the specific symptom cluster of severe night pain and swelling without systemic fever suggest an spondyloarthropathy. The X-ray requested will help rule out erosive changes or enthesitis.
